items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: one uncle I had, Uncle Willy, he had a colt... I said, 'I sure will, Uncle. I sure will.'

ctx.x: I took a second look and forgot all about Mr. Blunt into the love action. I said I need to go to school now. So I went down and went in. So she said, well, yes. You need an apartment. Well, everybody was living (inaudible) apartments, had those sunken bathtubs at that time, that was something else. Sunken bathtubs and mosaic floors and mosaic in the bathroom. And she said, "Well, I'm going to get you that and you won't have to worry about those Jeff Blunt or anyone else." And I said, well, why not.

So I moved down. But she would be away about three or four days. "Oh, I had to go downtown to see my folks and everything. And by the way, if you need this..." and give me a pearl handle automatic. "Because you're not big and your hands ain't big for fighting people." I said, "They're not." Because what I knew about them firearms, because one uncle I had, Uncle Willy, he had a colt, one of the longest colts I ever seen. And he wore it day and night. And he slept with this colt. And one night while he was…
person that took that $10.00 out of Uncle's bag, his belt, you tell him to put it right back in there and I will not tell his mother anything." I said, "I sure will, Uncle. I sure will."
